column1: # What Aminet software actually calls, and what each profile does to it.
# Filled by the standing survey.  A row is only written from INSTRUCTION-LEVEL
# proof: SocketBase resolved from its OpenLibrary store, then only
# `movea.l SocketBase,a6` / `jsr d16(a6)` pairs counted.  A raw `4E AE` scan
# over-counts about fivefold -- AmiFTP 1.843 really calls 18 vectors and the
# raw scan claimed 89 -- so a raw hit is never evidence.
# kind:    lvo      keyed by the api name in lvo-matrix.tsv
#          feature  something with no vector, keyed by its option
# status:  BREAKS   the profile stops the program working
#          DEGRADED the program runs but cannot do its job
#          CLEAN    proven NOT called, so the stub is free

column1: # Batch D and F, 2026-09-07.  Servers and mail clients.

column6: ungated in every profile; NOT universal -- net.lib init_inet_daemon() daemons (lpd, identd) never call it
no ROUTING/DNS/ADDRALLOC/NETMONITOR/NETSTATUS/ADDRINFO/BPF vector called by any of the seven; none does reverse DNS either, they log numeric addresses

AveHTTPD stores the bsdsocket AND AS225 socket.library base in the SAME global (0xfde0), a mode flag at 0xfddc selects. Proving SocketBase from its OpenLibrary store is NOT sufficient -- partition by the cmp #1/beq branch or the scan invents ProcessIsServer, GetRouteInfo, gethostbyaddr
gcc/ixemul daemons expose ZERO bsdsocket vectors; the whole contract lives inside ixemul.library. A vector scan files them CLEAN and is wrong

FIXED: was bsd_enosys in every profile, so telnetd's 4 calls, lpd's 8, AmiFTPd's 28+ and POPd's went nowhere on the default build too. Implemented via ami_log_raw() for about 250 bytes; the library already stored SBTC_LOGTAGPTR/LOGSTAT/LOGFACILITY and discarded the calls that used them

column1: # Batch E, 2026-09-07.  Browsers, download managers and IRC.

column6: SOCK_RAW IS recoverable after all: the type argument is a constant immediate at every socket() site in this corpus (socket(2,1,0) / (2,1,6) / pea 0,pea 1,pea 2). Decoding the arguments answers what the LVO table cannot, and would have caught AvePING

the single named cause of every false BREAKS: exec PutMsg/GetMsg/ReplyMsg/WaitPort (-366..-384) alias bpf_open/close/read/write, CloseLibrary(-414) aliases AddRouteTagList, CreatePool..FreePooled(-696..-714) alias ObtainServerSocket and the DNS group, AllocMem/FreeMem(-198/-210) alias Inet_MakeAddr/gethostbyname, dos Open..Input(-30..-54) alias socket/bind/listen/accept/connect, gadtools SetGadgetAttrsA(-42) aliases listen with 28 hits in HTTPResume alone
the naive scan reports getaddrinfo on HTTPResume, and that API postdates the corpus -- so the tripwire fires automatically and proves the scan wrong without a human noticing
eight binaries, SocketBase proven in every one, exhaustive slot enumeration rather than heuristics: zero calls to anything minimal stubs

smail_amitcp: ObtainSocket + Dup2Socket + vsyslog, the inetd daemon signature, re-verified after the a6-clobber fix. ConnectLine ships SIX daemons calling it -- CLChatD, CLChatIRCD, clfingerd, cltcpmond and two more -- so the pattern is a whole BBS suite rather than one program. DayDreamBBS's ftpd is the richest single binary found, 23 vectors including ObtainSocket, Dup2Socket and vsyslog
ELEVEN of sixty are ixemul-hosted and therefore invisible to any vector scan -- 18 per cent, not a rare case. Coverage figures overstate real coverage by roughly that much

tools/aminet-scan.py reported ONE vector for mail clients that plainly open sockets, so its absences mean nothing; its positives are still sound (zero false positives against hand-verified truth). CLEAN may never rest on it

movea.l <ea>,a6 spans 0x2C40..0x2C7F and only four forms are followed; every other one must CLEAR the tracked base. Leaving out 0x2C78 -- movea.l 4.w,a6, how every Amiga program fetches SysBase -- let exec calls inherit the socket base and put AddRouteTagList (-414 = exec CloseLibrary) into an email client's vector list four times

THE BARREN FRACTION IS A PROPERTY OF THE DRAWER, NOT OF comm/. Four passes read 91, 92, 93.5 and 92 per cent barren and the fifth reads 82: comm/dlg is a BBS package's data files, comm/irc is dense. 36 attributed binaries in 1,960 archives so far. The earlier extrapolation of ~146 for the whole 5,372 was drawn from four thin drawers in a row and is a FLOOR, not an estimate

the whole of comm/bbs, 400 archives scanned end to end, yields eleven attributed binaries calling 26 distinct vectors between them -- and lvo-matrix.tsv answers ok on default AND on minimal for all 26. A fifth independent slice, and the first one that is a complete Aminet directory rather than a sample

ddbbs ftpd calls the whole address-arithmetic quartet -- Inet_LnaOf, Inet_NetOf, Inet_MakeAddr, Inet_NtoA -- in one binary, the first instruction-level proof any of the three rarer ones is called at all. All four are ungated and ok in every profile

CNet BBS ships its own network suite -- telnet client, traceroute, IRC, SMTP/finger/ident daemons, an NNTP fetcher and a mailer -- 31 distinct vectors across the corpus so far and lvo-matrix.tsv answers ok on default AND minimal for every one. Micro fails ObtainSocket and ReleaseSocket and degrades gethostbyname, gethostbyaddr and gethostname

cnet4demo traceroute reports recvfrom, sendto and getprotobyname but NOT socket and NOT CloseSocket, which no working traceroute can manage. A second, sharper instance of the asymmetry row above: an attributed vector list is a FLOOR, never a total, and sock_raw=0 on that binary is therefore not evidence it opens no raw socket

the whole of comm/irc, 16 attributed binaries, 25 distinct vectors, and NOT ONE breaks micro -- no ObtainSocket, no ReleaseSocket, no SOCK_RAW. Only gethostbyname, gethostbyaddr and gethostname degrade to hosts-only. The first slice where micro itself is clean apart from names

EVERY IRC DAEMON IN THE CORPUS IS IXEMUL-HOSTED -- UnrealIRCd, epic4, eggdrop, bitlbee (four builds), BitchX, IRCServices, AmIRCD -- 34 of 400 archives, and a vector scan sees nothing in any of them. The server side of comm/irc is INVISIBLE to this method rather than absent from it, which the 18 per cent figure from the 60-archive screening understated for daemons specifically

HOW MUCH the a6-clobber fix was worth, measured rather than asserted: three archives from the 60-archive screening pass re-scanned here read AirMailPro 1 -> 7 vectors and AminetFileRequester 3 -> 8, while AEMail230 held at 7 as the control. Every `screened` row written before that fix is a floor by roughly that factor, which is why the gate refuses a CLEAN claim that cites one

the Roadshow interface-enumeration group -- ObtainInterfaceList, QueryInterfaceTagList, ReleaseInterfaceList -- is CALLED, by AmigaTText in both its 68k and WarpUP builds, 24 vectors each. First instruction-level proof for any of the three; all ungated, so `ok` in every profile including micro

the ONLY citation in the corpus, from FENStarter's arp. The netdb networks path stays ungated on that basis -- one caller in 2,793 archives is not nothing, and splitting it was already judged not worth a fortieth option at ~300 bytes
